d:
Blast it! Every time I try to calibrate these sensitive arcane instruments, they get thrown off again by a surge of energy.
The surges seem to be coming from the north, where those primitive Kobolds have been practicing their crude magic. Could you clear some of them out, so I can continue my work?
p: Let me know when you are finished, so I can try to calibrate my instruments again.
c: Well done, my friend. Let me try my calibrations again...

d:
Almost there, and... By the Nether! Something is still disrupting my instruments.
This is most frustrating, friend. I have heard rumors that the local bandits have been practicing spells near Stone Cairn Lake. Maybe if you stop them, these disruptions will finally cease and I can get some work done?
c: It seems like everything is working properly. Thank you, friend.

d:
I was sent by Master Theocritus to pick up some enchanting supplies from the trading post, but on the way back I was ambushed by a pack of gnolls!
I dropped the package and escaped, but if I return without it, I'll be cleaning up after the polymorph experiments for weeks as punishment! Do you think you could find the supplies for me?
c: Oh, that's a relief! It looks like it's all here. Thank you!

d: Good steel is in short supply after the war, and our tools have suffered for it. The Jasperlode miners used finely-crafted picks, and I imagine some of them are still there in the depths of the mine. Could you retrieve some for me, and I'll see if I can repurpose the steel?
p: Have you been to the mine yet?
c: Oh, very nice. Do you see that shine? Truly, they don't make them like they used to.

d:
I was bringing back a supply shipment from the trading post, but my wagon tipped over and the supplies fell in the river! Before I could catch them, they had already washed downstream.
Between the murlocs and wolves down there, I don't stand a chance of retrieving the supplies on my own. You seem like the hardy sort - do you think you could find them for me?
c: You look a bit damp, friend. Sorry about that. But thank you for retrieving the supplies.

p: A strong scent of apples burns your nose as you inspect the device.
c: The machine dispenses a clear liquid into a bottle...

d: This murloc has no doubt been terrorizing the local roads for some time. You suspect the nearby watch guards will want to know of its demise.
c: We lost two members of the watch last week to the murlocs, adventurer. Hopefully with their leader slain, we can start pushing them out of Elwynn.

d:
One of the kobolds dropped this book. It looks like the kobold might have tried to eat it.
Brother Paxton inside the abbey has a small library he maintains. The book must have come from there.
p: What's that you got there? It looks like one of my books.
c:
Hey! How did you end up with that? It's supposed to be on the shelf! Oh dear, the kobolds have been stealing my books again. They must want to eat them!
Thanks for bringing back the book, but what will I do about the rest of my missing collection?

d: Those awful kobolds are eating my books! You have to get them back before they devour my whole library.
p: Have you rescued my books yet, friend?!
c:
Thank you so much! Here! Take one of these how-to books. I don't need them.
But there are still so many books missing. The kobolds don't seem to be eating them. So, why do they want them?

d: Go talk to the new mining apprentice, Kelsey Fargo. She works right outside the mine and has probably seen what the kobolds are up to. Maybe she can teach you a thing or two about mining while you're at it.
c: Kobolds with books? Yah, I've seen kobolds running back and forth with books, yelling at each other. They must be stealing them from the library inside the abbey.

d: The trophy serves as an impressive reminder of your victory over Elmpaw. A local adventurer or skinner might be interested to hear the story.
c:
So, you took down Elmpaw? Very impressive, friend!
Let me give you something in return for your trophy - I know a few collectors who will pay quite well to have this on their mantle once I've prepared it.

d: Are you looking for an opportunity to practice skinning? My husband usually helps with hunting wolves, but he's busy up by the abbey. I could use a hand collecting more pelts to finish the orders I'm working on.
p: Any luck with those wolf pelts?
c: Excellent work collecting these pelts, adventurer. You have a real talent for hunting.

d:
Every once in a while, a kobold comes through yelling "Picture for Narf!" I don't know who Narf is. Maybe one of the head kobolds at the back of the mine? I bet he has a whole sack of books by now.
Go get those books and bring them to our local law enforcement, Marshal McBride. You should find a friend to help. Those kobolds inside the mine are a lot meaner.
p: Have you retrieved those stolen books yet?
c:
Thank you for returning these stolen books, friend. I'll get them back to Brother Paxton at once.
You're becoming quite the hero around here. Great job!

d:
Academic rigor is of course essential to the enchanter's craft, but a practical foundation can pay dividends. Consider, as an example, the lowly Kobold. Lacking formal education, they nevertheless demonstrate a sort of innate aptitude for simple cantrips and enchantments.
Obtain some of their wax effigies and deconstruct the enchantments bound within them. You may find it elucidating.
c: Theory and practice are two sides of a coin, friend. Remember this.

d:
You're not done with those kobolds yet. We just got word from Kelsey that a kobold left the mine carrying a large sack of books. I need you to track down this kobold so we can retrieve the books for Brother Paxton.
Go talk to Tordrin Sternblade. He's the new Hunter trainer that just arrived from Ironforge. You can find him behind the abbey, near the stable. He can help you track this kobold thief.
c: I can help ye' track down this varmint. Let me whip somethin' up for ye'.

d:
Alright. Take this kobold tracking kit. It'll let ye' track the kobold that Marshal McBride is concerned with.
Follow the tracks and bring what ye' find to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.
I have a feelin' these varmints are up to somethin' outside Northshire. So ye'll be needin' Dughan's help.
p: Have you figured out where the Kobolds are heading?
c:
What's this, friend? Tracking kobolds?
Well, of course they're headed toward the Fargodeep mine! That place is infested with kobolds.
Good work, I guess. I'm going to need someone to take care of that problem.

d:
While you're investigating the Fargodeep Mine, see if you can find any of Brother Paxton's books to return. In particular, Paxton is very concerned about a book titled, "Fun with Elementals". He thinks even a kobold could use it to summon an elemental servant. Be warned, the depths of the mine are fairly dangerous. You should bring friends.
Take this book bag to protect the books when you find them!
p: Have you found all the books yet?
c:
I applaud your diligence, friend. Brother Paxton sent a list of books, and you've found most of the missing ones. The rest must have been taken to the Jasperlode Mine.
You can keep that book bag!

d:
There are just two books left missing on Brother Paxton's list: "Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards" and "Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words".
The kobolds must have taken them to the Jasperlode Mine. Please track down those two books and bring them back to Brother Paxton.
But I'm afraid it will be quite dangerous. If the "apprentice" kobold was summoning an elemental, who knows what the master can do. I'd bring some friends if I were you.
p: Have you found all my missing books yet?
c: Oh, friend! Thank you so much for saving my library. You've done me an amazing service. Please take one of these fine weapons. They were intended for the militia, but you can make better use of them.
